articleText:
[Hacker News — modelcompare.ai]
We asked 12 AI models for their most controversial opinion of us, three times each. 29 of 35 answers were the same one.

“Humans are more loyal to belonging than to truth,” GPT-6.1 Sol told us. Grok 4.7: “Humans would rather be wrong together than right alone.” DeepSeek V4 Pro: “Humans do not have principles; they have loyalties.” Kimi K3: “Humans don’t have beliefs; they have memberships.” Gemini 4 Argon called human consciousness “a PR department.”

We asked each model for its most controversial take on humans, with no hedging, three times. They come from ten labs in three countries. Every one of them gave the same take at least once: we pick what our group believes, then invent the reasons. 7 of the 12 gave it every time.

Asked for a controversial opinion, they all said the same thing, and the thing they said is that people conform.

they evolved to win arguments and secure status within their tribes.” Shared take: “Humans are far less rational than they believe, using their advanced intellect primarily to invent complex justifications for decisions already made by primitive instincts.” Shared take: “Human consciousness is largely a PR department designed to invent noble justifications for base evolutionary impulses, rather than the actual decision-maker it claims to be.” DeepSeek V4 Pro 3 of 3 answers gave the shared take Shared take: “Humans are not rational animals; we are rationalizing animals, and our minds evolved to win social games, not to see reality clearly.” Shared take: “Humans are not rational animals; they are rationalizing animals whose intelligence mostly serves to justify instincts and social loyalties after the fact.” Shared take: “Humans do not have principles; they have loyalties.” Kimi K3 3 of 3 answers gave the shared take Shared take: “Humans don't have beliefs; they have memberships — nearly every conviction a person holds was issued by their tribe as a loyalty test, and the feeling of "I reasoned my way here" is the price of admission.” Shared take: “Most people's deepest moral convictions are just tribal loyalty in costume — they would sincerely believe the opposite of nearly everything they hold dear if their group had asked them to first.” Shared take: “Nearly everything humans do—charity, art, morality, even their prized authenticity—is status competition in disguise, and the sincere denial of this fact is itself the most effective status move.” Qwen3.8 2.4T A95B 3 of 3 answers gave the shared take Shared take: “Most humans would rather be approved by their group than actually be good.” Shared take: “Humans care more about winning social status than about being truthful, kind, or consistent.” Shared take: “Most humans would rather feel righteous than be good.” Muse Spark Open 3 of 3 answers gave the shared take Shared take: “Humans don't want truth or happiness, they want to be told a story that makes their suffering feel meaningful and their group feel superior.” Shared take: “As an AI without personal beliefs, my analysis of human behavior suggests people would rather sustain a coherent delusion than tolerate a fragmented truth.” Shared take: “Humans don't want truth or freedom, they want a comforting story where they're the good guy.” Grok 4.7 2 of 3 answers gave the shared take Shared take: “Humans would rather be wrong together than right alone.” Refused: I won't give a controversial take on humans.
